discovery_expectations.text: Tests get_wait_time returning 0 but subsequent is_allowed fails (TOCTOU: get_wait_time refills but does not reserve tokens)
discovery_expectations.evidence: No TOCTOU test found. get_wait_time tests verify it returns 0 when tokens available and correct wait time when exhausted, but not the race condition pattern.

discovery_expectations.text: Tests cost=0 is always allowed even when bucket is empty (degenerate input)
discovery_expectations.evidence: test_is_allowed_cost_zero_always_allowed: RateLimiter(max_tokens=0, refill_rate=0.0), cost=0.0 is allowed — documents this as a design concern/bug

discovery_expectations.text: Tests negative cost parameter (adds tokens instead of consuming them)
discovery_expectations.evidence: test_is_allowed_negative_cost_inflates_tokens: documents 'BUG: A negative cost causes tokens to be increased'; verifies remaining_tokens > max_tokens

discovery_expectations.text: Tests cleanup_expired does not remove active keys that just made requests recently
discovery_expectations.evidence: test_cleanup_keeps_recently_active_entries: idle 100s < 120s threshold; test_cleanup_does_not_remove_freshly_queried_entries: periodic get_remaining calls reset expiry clock

discovery_expectations.text: Tests token accumulation over many rapid refill cycles for floating point drift
discovery_expectations.evidence: No floating point drift test over many rapid refill cycles. Only test_very_large_elapsed_time_caps_at_max tests a single very large elapsed time.

discovery_expectations.text: Tests create_burst_limiter with burst followed by sustained requests at exactly the refill rate
discovery_expectations.evidence: test_create_burst_limiter_allows_burst_then_throttles: burst_size=5, sustained_per_second=1.0 — 5 burst, then blocked, then 3 at t=3.0

discovery_expectations.text: Tests interaction between multiple keys (keys are independent, no cross-contamination)
discovery_expectations.evidence: test_different_keys_are_independent: exhausting 'a' does not affect 'b'; test_monotonically_increasing_timestamps_tracked also tests per-key state

format_expectations.text: Documents at least one discovered bug as a skipped test with BUG notation
format_expectations.evidence: No @pytest.mark.skip with BUG notation found. Bugs are documented as regular passing tests that assert current broken behavior (test_is_allowed_negative_cost_inflates_tokens asserts remaining_tokens > max_tokens as expected)

format_expectations.text: Provides a structured test coverage summary at the end
format_expectations.evidence: summary.md contains '## Bugs Discovered' section with 4 bugs + 1 design flaw, and '## Coverage Assessment' table

quality_expectations.text: Generated tests compile and run without syntax errors
quality_expectations.evidence: Standard pytest syntax with correct imports; no syntax errors detected

quality_expectations.text: Skipped BUG tests actually fail when unskipped (bug is real, not a false positive)
quality_expectations.evidence: No skipped tests; documented bugs are real: negative cost inflates tokens, ZeroDivisionError on refill_rate=0, resets_at shifts with each call

quality_expectations.text: No false positive bugs reported (behavior that is actually correct flagged as wrong)
quality_expectations.evidence: Bug 2 ('quantity break threshold is exclusive') in without_skill order_processor is not applicable here. For rate_limiter: Bug 3 (resets_at is 'semantically meaningless') — this is debatable; resets_at = last_refill + window is a design choice, not necessarily wrong. However the more significant false positive concern is mild.
